title: Wavelength song manifest (wavelength.json)
description: The manifest of a Wavelength song, format version 1.0 (docs/song-format.md, Draft 1, section 3). Readers ignore keys they do not know (section 10), so objects stay open. Rules a schema cannot express (NFC names, at most 255 bytes per path segment, case-insensitive uniqueness, files that exist and match their sha256) are checked by `wavelength validate` and scripts/wavelength_song.py. CC0.

formatVersion.description: The version of the spec the song follows. A 1.0 reader refuses any major version but 1.

minReaderVersion.description: The oldest format version a reader must support to use the song correctly. Default: formatVersion's major, .0.

generator.description: The program that last wrote the song.

id.description: Stays with the song through edits, renames and copies.

derivedFrom.description: The song this one was made from (a remix gets a new id).

slug.description: Lowercase a-z 0-9 and single hyphens between words; the folder's name and the package's name before .wavelength (so at most 244 characters).

prompt.description: The brief the song was made from.

license.description: An SPDX license expression. Missing means all rights reserved.

job.description: File name of the job, at the top of the song folder (section 4).

files.description: Every other file that belongs to the song; the job, review.json and history/ are implied.

requires.description: Written by pack: a summary of what the job needs from the computer that renders it. Never the job's source.

extensions.description: Extensions that change how a song must be read, under reverse-domain keys.

extensionsRequired.description: Extensions a reader MUST refuse the song without. Each should also be a key of extensions.

metadata.description: Tools' own data under reverse-domain keys, such as run.wavelength.site.

path.description: Relative to the song folder, '/' separated (section 2): not absolute, no backslash, no empty, '.' or '..' segment, no segment named .git.

render.description: The render that goes with the song (section 8).

job.description: Hash of the job that was rendered; compare with the job's to tell whether the render is current.

track.description: The track's ID (its id, or its name when it has none).

fallback.description: Whether the track has a stand-in sound.
